name: A factoring membrane that receives a semiprime N alone and discovers its factors by carrying the same correlated factor/product/carry relation through successive IMASM dialects. It finds a route whose rules make the relationship between N and its factors explicit and usable for extraction. Each dialect transforms the state returned by the preceding dialect. Nested re-entry preserves and composes the resulting alternatives, while enclosing banks retain their correlations across reversal. Returned constraints feed back into that same resident relation until a proper divisor emerges. The complete source-bound computational state is prepared and baked into a self-contained executable. Execution triggers the prepared membrane and emits its terminal result when the divisor, derived quotient, zero remainder, exact product N, and paired boundary close together.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary that contains the entire factoring computation; all five closure conditions must hold simultaneously for the membrane to emit its terminal result and halt production.

≻.chosen_element: forward dialect hop — U22 join, U26 join, U67 tensor transformation
≻.justification: Each dialect in the native route (U22→U26→U67) transforms the correlated factor/product/carry tuple returned by the preceding dialect, advancing the computation toward factor emergence.

≺.chosen_element: constraint feedback and rollback — returned support masks, quotient/remainder evidence, frame contractions feeding back into the resident relation

⋈.chosen_element: sequential dialect composition — each dialect acts on the tuple returned by the preceding dialect across all twelve coordinates

⊙.chosen_element: self-contained executable membrane — the baked preparation that knows its own factor/product/carry relation

∋.chosen_element: common-consequence fuse — unions surviving row and pair alternatives, then contracts the returned shared state
∋.justification: After nested re-entry explores alternatives, FFUSE reunites the T-arm (surviving candidates) and F-arm (eliminated candidates) by union of surviving alternatives, then applies pair contraction and frame contraction to restrict the common wire register.

⊥.chosen_element: negative arm — a factor-bit alternative eliminated by constraint violation or interval bound exclusion
⊥.justification: The F-arm carries factor-bit assignments that conflict with the source inverse-product operation, native division bounds, or admitted shared-row pairs; it is pruned by pair contraction.
